qt: to the Commission Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI) Subject:

School transport presents a long-standing problem, which parents and pupils have had to deal with once again since the start of the new school year. Months after reopening their gates, many schools across the country have been left without a complete transport service as contractors do not consider them to be an ‘attractive prospect’, leaving it to private companies to fill the gap and, in many cases, to parents to organise and cover the cost of their children’s daily transport. These issues are only addressed – and with piecemeal and patchy solutions at that – following pressure and protests from parents, teachers and pupils. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What view does it take of the fact that, year after year, the safe and unhindered transport of pupils remains ‘up in the air’ and dependent on the renewal of NSRF programmes for funding, as well as on whether or not contractors take part in the relevant tenders on the basis of their expected profit?

What view does it take of the need to end the dependence of school transport on private transport providers by creating a public body for each region with permanent state funding, purchasing all the necessary vehicles, and hiring permanent drivers and specialised vehicle attendants, so that each and every journey needed to transport pupils is planned and carried out in a safe and timely manner?
